currentContext.business: Omnitech manufactures highly engineered precision machined components and assemblies (weight 0.003 kg to 503.33 kg, precision up to 5 microns) majorly used in safety-critical applications. With 19 years of experience it supplied over 256 customers across 24 countries during FY23-H1FY26, deriving the majority of revenue from exports (~75%). Products serve Energy (oil & gas, wind, power), Motion Control & Automation, Industrial Equipment Systems and other diversified industrial applications.
currentContext.expansion: Setting up two new manufacturing facilities (Proposed Facility 1 & 2) at Chhapara, Lodhika, Rajkot via civil construction/interior development and purchase of equipment/machinery, plus rooftop solar and new machinery at Existing Facility 2; the company has also acquired three land parcels with potential built-up area of 44,450.99 sq m in Chhapara to partially de-risk future growth.

one-line thesis: Omnitech Engineering has transitioned from a steady grower to a high-visibility compounder, securing a ~INR 3,000 Cr order book (up from INR 283 Cr in FY25) driven by multi-year MPAs with global oilfield giants like Weatherford. While Q4 margins faced temporary compression due to pre-investment costs and inventory build-up for ramp-up, the de-levered balance sheet and new capacity commissions position the firm for sustained 30-35% CAGR through FY28.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 511.3 Cr (+49.1% YoY); Q4 Rev: INR 148.7 Cr (+38.5% YoY). EBITDA: INR 171.1 Cr (+45.4% YoY); Margin: 33.5% (FY26) vs 34.3% (FY25); Q4 Margin dipped to 33.4% (-450 bps QoQ) due to front-loaded opex. PAT: INR 79.3 Cr (+80.9% YoY); Margin 15.5%. Order Book: ~INR 3,000 Cr (as of May 25, 2026) vs INR 283 Cr (FY25 end), includes INR 900 Cr Weatherford MPA. Net Debt/Equity: 0.34x (improved from 1.6x in FY25) post-IPO equity infusion. One-offs: Q4 margin pressure from strategic hiring/capex prep; Inventory days elevated due to MOQ commitments for new programs.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 30-35% expected for FY27 (in line with historical trend). Margins: Expected to revert to historical levels (~34% EBITDA) post-Q4 aberration. Order Inflow: Strong pipeline in Aerospace/Defense; repeat business >90% in non-energy segments. Capex/Commissioning: New Hyderabad facility (leased, defense-focused) and Chhapara expansion commissioning post-Q1 FY27; Ahmedabad land acquired for FY29+ growth.
order book & pipeline: Total ~INR 3,000 Cr; Mix: Energy 74% (led by INR 900 Cr Weatherford 5-year MPA), Motion & Automation 14%, Industrial Equipment 12%. Geography: North America 64%, Asia 34%, India 1.5%. Ramp-up: Gradual over 5 years for major MPAs (e.g., Weatherford), with significant revenue contribution starting FY27.
segment / subsidiary detail: Energy (53% of rev, 74% of order book) driven by oilfield services (Weatherford, SLB, Halliburton). Motion Control (25% of rev) and Industrial Equipment (16% of rev) show high repeatability (>90%). Aerospace emerging with AS9100 certification and NADCAP in-progress; 4 FA development orders received.
growth verticals / optionality: Aerospace & Defense vertical scaling (Titanium/Inconel machining, sub-assemblies); Geographic diversification beyond North America (Europe/UK initiatives); Value-add expansion into testing and full assemblies; Capacity headroom expanding from 2.6M to >4M machine hours by FY29.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA margin compression (19.7% PAT margin held, but EBITDA margin dipped) attributed to front-loaded costs for FY27 growth (hiring, prep). Raw material cost pass-through is effective (ex-works model); no significant lag. Margins expected to normalize to historical ~34% EBITDA as revenue scales into new capacity.
capex / expansion: Strategic expansion: 1) New leased facility in Hyderabad (defense proximity); 2) Chhapara plant expansion (IPO funded); 3) Solar roofing at Chhapara. Total machine hour capacity to double from 2.6M to >4M by FY29. Land acquired in Ahmedabad for future beyond-FY28 needs.
capital allocation: De-leveraging priority achieved (Net Debt/Equity 0.34x). IPO proceeds utilized for capacity expansion and working capital. Focus on balancing growth capex with liquidity; GST credit of INR 24.3 Cr expected to realize in FY27, boosting cash flows.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on massive order book ramp-up; Talent retention in Rajkot vs. new geographies; Geopolitical disruptions in Middle East (though minimal impact noted so far); Certification delays in Aerospace could slow diversification; Working capital strain (Receivable days 153, Inventory build-up) during ramp-up phase.
management quality / tone: Confident and execution-focused; emphasizes 'conscious' order booking aligned with capacity ramp; transparent about Q4 margin blip being temporary; highlights strong ecosystem in Rajkot mitigating talent concerns.
non-obvious takeaways: The INR 3,000 Cr order book is not immediate revenue but a 5-year ramp, reducing execution shock; >90% of non-energy revenue is repeat business, providing a stable base while energy scales; Aerospace entry is via 'development orders' first, indicating a structured, low-risk qualification path before full production.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for reliable, high-precision Tier-1 suppliers outside China for oilfield majors | Weatherford International | beneficiary | High | Secured INR 900 Cr MPA with Omnitech for 5-year supply, leveraging India's cost arbitrage and Omnitech's AS9100/NADCAP readiness. |
| Scaling aerospace component sourcing with certified Indian partners | Global Aerospace OEMs (Undisclosed) | beneficiary | Med | Omnitech's new certifications and development orders position it as a key beneficiary of aerospace supply chain shifts, though revenue impact is longer-term. |
| Margin pressure from raw material volatility | Unorganized Local Machining Units | loser | Low | Lack of ex-works pricing power and certification barriers make smaller players unable to compete with Omnitech's structured pass-through mechanisms. |

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: One of India's fastest-growing manufacturers of high-precision engineered components and assemblies for safety-critical applications, supplying global customers across energy, motion control & automation and industrial equipment systems.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Started in FY2007, Omnitech is one of the key manufacturer of high precision engineered components & assemblies" - 19 years in operation, with stated precision levels up to 5 Microns (0.005mm).
- Export-led business: ~78% of revenue from outside India (for the quarter ended June 30, 2026), over 256 global customers and sales in 24 countries (for the quarter/year ended June 30, 2026 and the last two fiscals).
- Certification stack is presented as the entry barrier: ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001, ISO 45001:2018, AS9100:2016 (for Aviation, Space & Defence), IATF 16949:2016 for Existing Facility 1, and American Petroleum Institute API Spec Q1 / API 20J / API 7-1 / API 5CT for Existing Facility 2.
- Marquee client credential named in the deck is Halliburton Energy Services, Inc., under the Energy sub-segment (Oil & Gas, Wind Energy and Power Sector).
- Recognition history includes Supplier Excellence Awards from Dover Corporation (2019, 2020, 2021), the Soaring Eagle Award from John Bean Technologies Corporation, a Best Supplier Award (Silver) from Power Build (2015-16), and in 2026 "2 Golds + 1 Silver Awards from CII-Institute of Quality Bengaluru under 21st CII National level 3M Kaizen competition".

Serves customers via a global delivery model with a Houston warehouse.

demand_drivers.body:

- Order book growth (Rs 17,647.84 million) concentrated in Energy (74.07%) driving forward visibility
- Customer concentration: top 10 customers 47.87% of FY25 product/service revenue
- Repeat-customer revenue share (FY25 ~79.78%) supporting revenue durability

commitments.body:

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:

- Deepen export presence and global delivery model
- Develop manufacturing-automation software through subsidiary Novatro Techsolutions

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Accounting change] The deck repeatedly flags that "PBT for Q1 FY27 includes an impact of change in depreciation method (WDV to SLM) effective this quarter"; depreciation and amortisation expense is shown at 62.7 INR Mn in Q1 FY27 versus 105.0 in Q1 FY26 and 134.7 in Q4 FY26.
- [Corporate structure] Novatro Techsolutions Private Limited was incorporated in FY2025; Omnitech Group Inc. is the US subsidiary operating the Houston warehouse. The Company was formerly Omnitech Engineering Private Limited and was "initially incorporated as a partnership firm under the name M/s Omnitech Engineering".
- [Milestones] Entered the Energy sector in FY2016; established Existing Facility 2 (stated in both the FY2018 and FY2024 milestones); revenue from operations crossed Rs 1,000.00 million in FY2022.
- [Governance] Promoter-led board and management - Udaykumar Arunkumar Parekh (Chairman and Managing Director), Paras Mukundrai Parekh (Whole-Time Director and CFO), Dharmi A Parekh (Non-Executive Director), with a COO recruited from Praj Industries/Thermax/L&T backgrounds and four independent directors.
